key_insight: PerovAgent autonomously designs ligands for halide perovskite nanocrystals while turning search observations into statistically testable chemical design principles.
engineering_relevance: The framework could guide surface-ligand engineering for perovskite materials, though solar-cell performance gains are not demonstrated in the abstract.
method: Combine LLM-driven multi-agent reasoning with atomistic model construction and machine-learned interatomic potentials.
Adaptively search ligand chemistries to improve binding energies on CsPbBr3 surfaces.
Validate proposed design principles statistically and examine a recurring alkynyl-phosphonate preference using density functional theory.
evidence_signal: Across 10 independent campaigns, 19 of 35 proposed principles received prospective support, seven also passed a confound audit, and DFT reproduced the alkynyl-phosphonate energetic preference.
watch_item: Limited survival through confound auditing underscores the need to validate LLM-generated hypotheses before using them as general design rules.
paper_title: PerovAgent: Autonomous Ligand Design for Halide Perovskite Nanocrystals
